name: Matrix multiplication exponent omega=2
question: Is the matrix multiplication exponent exactly two?
first_attack: Audit precise statement and prove a restricted case
dispatch_next: Import one published exact decomposition, such as a cited rank-23 scheme for the <3,3,3> tensor, and replay it on the tensor checker. A flip-graph search is not the next step: small formats cannot beat the laser-method bounds the blocker cites.
dispatch_why: Import a published decomposition onto the existing checker. The blocker says a small-format search cannot beat laser-method bounds below 2.372.

campaign.hypothesis: The exponent of matrix multiplication equals 2.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Replay published small-format decompositions (rank-23 <3,3,3> and recent flip-graph or learned schemes) as exact certificates and record the implied exponent bounds.
campaign.next_experiment: Add a JSON import path and a flip-graph rank-reduction search over small formats, with every candidate replayed by the exact checker.
campaign.falsification: Not finitely falsifiable: omega is a limit, and certified decompositions only give upper bounds.
campaign.blocker: Small-format ranks cannot beat laser-method bounds below 2.372; the probe is certificate infrastructure.

probes.name: Matrix multiplication exponent omega=2
probes.title: Exact matrix-multiplication tensor decompositions (Strassen and Kronecker powers)
probes.frontier: Known: omega <= log2(7) ~ 2.807 (Strassen 1969); the best published bounds are below 2.372 via the laser method. rank<2,2,2> = 7 exactly (Winograd 1971).

smoke.scope: Exact integer rank-7^k decompositions of the <2^k,2^k,2^k> matmul tensor for k in {1, 2}, hence omega <= log2(7).

deep.scope: Exact integer rank-7^k decompositions of the <2^k,2^k,2^k> matmul tensor for k in {1, 2, 3}, hence omega <= log2(7).

milestones.title: Strassen rank-7 <2,2,2> and rank-49 <4,4,4> decompositions checked exactly
milestones.scope: Classical upper bound omega <= log2 7; not new
milestones.description: Sparse exact expansion over Z matches the matrix multiplication tensor coefficient by coefficient; the deep run adds the rank-343 <8,8,8> Kronecker cube.
